lesson.menu_title: Getting Around the City -- Back in New York
lesson.menu_desc: A busy morning in Manhattan: ask a New Yorker for directions, understand a subway service change, and say what is normal for you with be used to and get used to ('I'm used to driving' / 'I'm getting used to the subway') -- 35 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 25 -- Getting Around the City
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Lucimara | Lesson 25 -- Getting Around the City
lesson.grammar_point: be used to / get used to (+ -ing)

listenings.text: Attention, passengers. This weekend, there is a service change on the seven line. From Friday at eleven p.m. to Monday at five a.m., seven trains will not stop at Fifth Avenue. Customers for Fifth Avenue should get off at Grand Central and walk two blocks west. Also, the elevator at the Times Square station is out of service until Sunday. Customers who need an elevator should use the entrance on Forty-First Street. During off-peak hours, trains are running every eight minutes. For more information, please speak to a station agent or check the MTA app. Thank you for riding with us.

Five years ago, I moved from Curitiba to New York, and my first month was hard. I wasn't used to walking so much, and I got lost almost every day. But you get used to it, and fast. Here are my three tips. First, learn the grid. In Manhattan, the avenues go north and south, and the streets go east and west. When someone gives you an address, always ask for the cross street. Second, travel off-peak when you can. At eight in the morning, the subway is full, but at ten, you can sit down and read. Third, on a nice day, take a bike-share bike along the Hudson River. It is the best view of the city, and it is cheap. And one more thing: avoid the restaurants in Times Square. Most of them are tourist traps. Today, I'm used to the noise and the crowds, and honestly, I love them.

extra_audio.text: First, I check the address and ask for the cross street. Then, I check the MTA app for service changes this weekend. Next, I take the train off-peak, when it is not so crowded. After that, I get off at the right stop and walk the last two blocks. Finally, I find a good place to eat, far from the tourist traps.
